description: Figure 16 is a grouped bar chart illustrating the average Shapley values for three multilingual language models — mBERT (light blue), XLM-R (dark blue), and chLSTM (light green) — across different relative positions to a probed target word. The horizontal axis categorizes positions as L₄₊ (four or more tokens to the left), L₃, L₂, L₁ (immediately to the left), T (the target word itself), R₁ (immediately to the right), R₂, R₃, and R₄₊ (four or more tokens to the right). The vertical axis, labeled “Shapley value,” ranges from 0 to 80, with major gridlines at intervals of 20. The chart shows that the highest Shapley values for all three models occur at position T (the target word), with chLSTM reaching approximately 78, XLM-R around 55, and mBERT near 60. Values drop sharply for positions immediately adjacent to the target (L₁ and R₁), and are near zero for positions further away (L₃, L₄₊, R₃, R₄₊). The bars for each position are grouped together by model, with consistent color coding as indicated in the legend in the upper right. The caption clarifies that these values are averaged over 247 tasks.
